direction: up only, from his face on the water toward where her head would be — two steps, and it never gets there
speed: about +18° in 0.5 s, hold 0.7 s, then a second +20° in 0.5 s, and the last 1.3 s held short of her; roughly 38° of tilt in total, no pan and no height change
angle: starts level on his face, ends about 38° up and still short of her face
start_frame: Water level on his face: the White Rabbit sitting back on his haunches, the waterline cutting the bottom of frame, his reflection doubled beneath him.
end_frame: The frame stopped far short of her: nothing in it but the wall of her skirt and shoulder running out of the top of frame, his exact eyeline aimed past the top edge at a head the camera never reaches — and because her bulk fills the whole upper frame, no vault and no lamp fitting is anywhere in shot.
constraint_honoured: 'The episode's ONE two-step camera move… runs out of room before it ever finds her face' — and the cinematography handoff's rule that the tilt must run out before any lamp fixture enters frame, which her own body guarantees here.
movement_note: Licensed move (c). One movement type only — a tilt; the two steps are a speed curve, not a second move. The 3.5 s duration (up from 3.0 s at shot-planning) exists precisely to give the stop-and-go its room.
